transcript:
Header: 2026-10-27 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Acme Head of ML), Sam Rodriguez (Acme SRE), Dana Lee (Product), Leo Ng (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (brief): decide model pin for POC, verify latency on Dedicated, prepare rollback/fallback plan, share security docs.

Topics: model selection, pinning, quantization tradeoffs, latency/throughput, fallback/rollbacks, security checklist (SOC2/KMS/SSO).

[00:00] Alicia Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll run through the latest benchmark we sent and then talk pinning and fallback strategy, Marco will jump in on the technicals.
[00:18] Priya Patel: thanks, Alicia. quick note - we got the spreadsheet but some columns are kinda swapped, so if you can highlight the p50/p95 rows that'd help.
[00:27] Alicia Chen: yes noted, we'll re-export - Marco, can you start with the throughput/latency summary?
[00:32] Marco Rivera: yeah sure, so in the last run we compared three variants: Llama-3-70B fp16, Llama-3-70B int4 quant, and a lightweight 13B for edge low-latency. the int4 gave about 35-40% cost reduction but p95 went up ~120ms in our Dedicated profile. p50 is still comparable.
[00:55] Sam Rodriguez: when you say Dedicated profile, is that our reserved pool config? what GPU type was it?
[01:02] Marco Rivera: yep this is on the dedicated A100-like pool we spun up for you; config uses 2x A100 80GB equivalent. sequence len was 512 tokens typical.
[01:14] Priya Patel: ok, so int4 is attractive cost-wise, but worried about tail latency. our SLAs are strict for checkout flows.
[01:22] Marco Rivera: totally, that's where pinning plus fallback comes in — we can pin most traffic to the int4 quant model but route high-priority routes or long-seq requests to the fp16 model, or do automatic fallback on p95 breach.
[01:36] Dana Lee: can you explain pinning — like how would rollbacks work in practice?
[01:40] Marco Rivera: sure - pinning is essentially mapping a route in the Redwood config to a specific model version. rollback is a config change to remap to previous version; we also support Canary/A-B and automatic fallback policies that detect regressions and shift traffic. changes are near-instant, but warmup of KV cache may add a small latency spike for the first few requests.
[02:02] Priya Patel: and cache warmup - how long are we talking? a minute? 5 minutes?
[02:07] Marco Rivera: usually a minute-ish for typical chat sessions; for very long contexts it can be a few minutes. that's why we recommend gradual pinning during business hours, and pre-warming with synthetic traffic if you expect a big shift.
[02:21] Priya Patel: good call. also for accuracy/regression we've got our eval set — if we pin to int4 we need to run evals to check for hallucination regressions.
[02:30] Alicia Chen: exactly - we've tied Redwood Optimize evals to pinning workflows; we can run your eval set nightly and alert on quality drift.
[02:39] Leo Ng: quick infra question - if we do fallback to fp16, are we billed for both models simultaneously or only when fallback triggers?
[02:45] Marco Rivera: cost-wise you pay for the inference consumed; if both are active you pay for both. for Dedicated you can configure a smaller standby pool for the fp16 fallback to reduce cost but still keep cold-start low.
[02:59] Sam Rodriguez: sounds like the standby pool is an ops tradeoff we need to size. can Redwood provide recommended sizing?
[03:05] Marco Rivera: yes, we'll include recommended pool sizes based on your QPS and the p95 targets — that's in the spreadsheet.

[03:18] Priya Patel: on model catalog naming — we saw a few different labels, "Redwood-70B-v1" vs "llama-3-70b-quant" — I'd prefer we standardize the pin names in the config so product folks don't get confused.
[03:29] Alicia Chen: agreed. we'll send a cleaned mapping table: human-friendly route name -> catalog id -> suggested pin.

[03:37] Dana Lee: any thoughts on rollbacks during business hours vs off-hours? we can't have flapping.
[03:42] Marco Rivera: recommended pattern is canary for 10% during low traffic, monitor p95/err rate for 30m, then ramp. automatic rollback triggers for quality regressions are available but we usually suggest manual for first few rollouts.

[03:58] Priya Patel: security ask — Priya: we need SOC2 docs, KMS integration details, and whether keys stay in our cloud KMS. also SSO for Console.
[04:08] Alicia Chen: yep we'll share SOC2 report and KMS integration guide. for Private deployments keys can remain in your KMS; for Dedicated we integrate with partner KMS/HSM. SSO via SAML is supported.
[04:20] Sam Rodriguez: can we get an architecture diagram that shows network egress and VPC peering?
[04:25] Alicia Chen: yes, we'll attach network diagram and a sample firewall/policy doc.

[04:33] Leo Ng: curious about eval latency — you mentioned p95 up by 120ms on int4, what were absolute numbers?
[04:38] Marco Rivera: p50 ~ 160ms, p95 ~ 420ms for int4; fp16 p95 ~ 300ms on the same workload. that was with 512 token sequences and batching at QPS 80.
[04:52] Priya Patel: that's borderline for checkout. if we move critical routes to fp16 maybe that'll be fine. we want to aim for p95 < 350ms for checkout.
[05:01] Marco Rivera: understood — recommendation: pin checkout route to fp16 with a 1.5x overhead buffer, pin chat/FAQ to int4. set fallback policy to route to fp16 on p95 > 350ms for 15m window.
[05:15] Alicia Chen: we'll document that policy in the playbook and include an example config snippet.

[05:23] Dana Lee: what about testing pin changes — can we do a staged rollout in the POC cluster?
[05:28] Marco Rivera: yes, we can show you a staged rollout in the POC; can do canary + auto rollback demo next week.

[05:34] Priya Patel: perfect. on next steps, please include the quantized model artifacts and a short note on known failure modes (like numbers getting truncated, tokenization issues).
[05:44] Marco Rivera: will do. also we'll add notes about KV cache warmup and how to pre-warm.

[05:50] Sam Rodriguez: on instrumentation, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards so we can set alerts. is that available out of box?
[05:58] Alicia Chen: yes Redwood Console has per-route metrics and can export token-cost breakdowns; we'll share dashboard links and a sample alert rule.

[06:07] Priya Patel: last thing — do you support fallback to smaller model instead of fp16? like 13B for extreme tail latency?
[06:12] Marco Rivera: you can configure multi-tier fallback: primary -> quantized large -> fp16 large -> 13B small. fallback logic can be latency-based or error-based.

[06:23] Alicia Chen: ok recap: Redwood to send cleaned spreadsheet + recommended pin mapping + playbook with rollback/fallback examples + security docs + network diagram. Acme to run Dedicated latency tests and share results. schedule canary demo next week.
[06:39] Priya Patel: sounds good thanks.
[06:41] Dana Lee: thanks everyone.
[06:42] Alicia Chen: great, we'll follow up with docs and schedule a canary demo. thanks all.

End of transcript.
